html:
The Yagalingu are an Aboriginal Australian people of inland central Queensland, in the upper Belyando River country. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their language may have been a dialect of Bidjara, spoken by their neighbours to the south. Little else is recorded of them. Other neighbours on the map include the Wangan, the Gayiri and the Iningai. Sheep and cattle runs spread across this country in the 1860s, after the colony of Queensland opened its inland to settlers. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
